question_scope: gameplay, shared-state, engine-interface, and reconstruction relevance

method: Read the committed source files and hash them with SHA-256 before deriving findings.

Parse functions.tsv, sdk_functions.tsv, both triage JSONL snapshots, the external allowlist, the xref TSV, the xref summary, the semantic atlas, the scope-488 extract, and the existing 121-row range audit.
Recompute canonical address sets, delta address sets, duplicate counts, SDK boundary counts, xref joins, caller-category context, queue references, and bounded static reachability.
Treat names, category labels, and xrefs as evidence of representation or caller context only; do not infer original gameplay semantics from an external API name.
Use the committed Ghidra manifest and addendum for the historical manager count; do not substitute a new live row export because the current bridge has no open program.
Sort all report maps and lists deterministically and omit wall-clock fields.

historical_partial_audit_reconciliation.reconciliation: The partial audit is a bounded subset of the full 488-row atlas, not an additional cause or a competing denominator.

gameplay_impact_artifact.interpretation: The full-row historical impact index agrees with the independent joins: seven external targets have gameplay-category caller adjacency, nine have bounded host/engine-boundary adjacency, and none is a gameplay logic body, shared-state root, or package anchor.

identity_and_counts.delta_address_space: EXTERNAL address space; not a numeric executable VA in .text

actual_distinct_executable_internal_func.basis: unique canonical VAs in functions.tsv and triage-v6

canonical_duplicate_names.interpretation: Duplicate names are not duplicate functions; the VA remains unique.

delta_duplicate_entries.semantic_equivalence: UNOBSERVABLE; external implementation bodies are not present

known_delta_name_matches_in_canonical_ex.interpretation: Name equality is not address or body identity; these are external entries with a name collision, not duplicate functions.

external.basis: all atlas rows have external=true and external address-space entries; xref export uses external reference type for DLL targets

import_identity.basis: known rows carry EXT:<DLL>::<name>; unknown rows retain external=true but no name or DLL

stub.basis: no stub flag or implementation body in the committed records

gameplay_logic.basis: delta rows are category UNKNOWN, outside the canonical gameplay universe, and lack bodies/contracts/runtime evidence

proven: All 488 delta records are external manager entries.
360 delta entries have an EXT DLL/name identity in the committed external allowlist.
The xref export contains 5481 external reference edges to 362 allowlisted external targets.
disproven: The 488 rows are not classified as internal thunk functions in the committed atlas: is_thunk is null for all 488.
The 4074 thunk xref edges are not an extra-function count and do not identify any of the 488 as a thunk.
unobservable: The external implementation body and whether Ghidra materialized any manager representation internally as a thunk cannot be inspected because the current program is not open and the atlas has no body.
cause_findings.conclusion: External import/manager scope is proven; a thunk explanation is not supported for the exact exported delta rows, while live-manager internals remain unobservable.

proven: The 488 delta Ghidra addresses and 488 EXTERNAL addresses are each unique.
The 58757 canonical function addresses are unique.
The 360 known external names are unique.
disproven: No duplicate delta entry or same-address duplicate is present in the committed reconciliation.
unobservable: Semantic equivalence or implementation duplication among external APIs cannot be determined from names and manager entries alone.
cause_findings.conclusion: The count difference is not a same-address duplicate set in the committed export.

proven: The 488 records carry no function body, body size, containing section, containing block, or generated classification.
The canonical export separately contains 178 thunk-flagged internal functions, but none is in the delta.
unobservable: Whether the manager's external entries are synthetic placeholders, import thunks, or other Ghidra bookkeeping cannot be established without a fresh row-level live manager export.
cause_findings.conclusion: Generated/compiler artifacts are not evidenced as the cause; they remain an unobservable live-representation possibility.

proven: No delta row has a body or body range from which tail containment could be tested.
The separate SDK boundary artifact contains 141 adjudicated tail-alias rows, proving that tail-alias analysis exists elsewhere in the corpus but not in this delta.
disproven: No delta row is recorded as a tail function or as an internal function alias.
unobservable: The external manager rows have no executable bytes or internal containing function to inspect for a tail.
cause_findings.conclusion: Tail functions do not explain the 488 exported entries; the separate 141 SDK tail aliases must not be conflated with this count.

proven: All 488 rows have external=true, canonical=false, and an EXTERNAL address-space entry.
The known 360 rows join to the external allowlist and account for 5479 external xref edges.
The remaining 128 rows are explicitly identity-unknown external entries, not internal function VAs.
disproven: They are not missing internal binary function entries by address in the committed canonical corpus.
unobservable: The semantics and implementation of the external DLL functions are outside the exported body corpus.
cause_findings.conclusion: External-only manager scope is the directly supported cause of the 59245-versus-58757 count difference.

proven: The delta entries run from EXTERNAL:00000001 through EXTERNAL:000001e8 and are in the EXTERNAL address space.
The canonical functions are 58757 unique .text VAs and have zero address overlap with the delta.
disproven: The delta is not a set of additional addresses inside the canonical .text range.
cause_findings.conclusion: The discrepancy is a representation/address-space scope difference, not 488 newly located internal binary VAs.

proven: The historical addendum records an analyzed SporeApp.exe manager count of 59245 and an in-memory iterator count of 58757.
The current bridge exposes zero open programs; a fresh manager row list and current program metadata cannot be read.
unobservable: Whether the historical manager had stale external state, and whether a fresh manager would produce the same 488 identities, cannot be tested without reopening or re-reading the program.
cause_findings.conclusion: Stale state is a live limitation, not a demonstrated cause. The count is retained as historical evidence only.

proven: functions.tsv, triage-v6, and the historical triage snapshot each contain 58757 rows with identical VA sets.
All checked binary-bearing artifacts carry the same binary SHA-256.
triage-v6 and the historical triage snapshot differ in classifier labels and counts, not in universe membership.
disproven: A classifier or snapshot version difference does not create 488 additional canonical VAs.
The 488 external-only rows are present in the committed semantic atlas associated with the same binary identity.
unobservable: A different Ghidra program state or export not present in the corpus could have a different manager representation.
cause_findings.conclusion: Snapshot/version drift is disproven for the committed corpus; it does not account for the count.

proven: The vtable scan reports 58756 internal functions, one below the 58757 canonical export, while the vtable candidates are 3081 data candidates and not a second executable universe.
sdk_functions.tsv has 1666 rows but 1663 unique addresses; 477 have exact canonical functions and 1186 do not.
The SDK repair artifact covers exactly those 1186 gaps: 848 repaired-contained, 193 dead-address, 141 tail-alias, 2 data/vtable-slot, and 2 prologue-recoverable.
The xref exporter records all callers as pinned and represents external targets by EXT tokens rather than EXTERNAL manager addresses.
disproven: The vtable count difference and the SDK exact-address gap are not the 488 manager-entry delta.
The 1186 SDK gaps are not the 488 external-only entries; their address sets are separate and the 488 have no executable body range.
unobservable: Whether any SDK gap ultimately represents behavior not reconstructable from its containing function requires separate semantic work; the current audit does not promote those rows.
cause_findings.conclusion: The corpus contains real analysis-boundary differences, but they are orthogonal to the 488 count.

proven: The canonical delta is zero: all 58757 canonical VAs are present in the committed function export and historical live observation reports all resolve.
The external delta is a set of manager entries outside the canonical executable VA universe.
There is a separate exact-address SDK gap of 1186 addresses, adjudicated by the SDK boundary artifact rather than by this manager delta.
disproven: The 488 discrepancy is not evidence of 488 missing internal SporeApp.exe functions.
The two WS2_32 allowlist targets absent from the 488 explain only two of the 5481 external xref edges and do not establish missing executable functions.
unobservable: The original implementation behind each external API is not reconstructed by this corpus and is not an internal missing-function question.
cause_findings.conclusion: Keep 58757 as the executable-function denominator and report 488 separately as external manager scope.

delta_reference_join.unknown_delta_derived_edges: UNOBSERVABLE because no identity join exists
delta_reference_join.source_field_discrepancy: The atlas external_xref_count=0 is not the derived xref count for the 360 allowlist-known rows; the derived join is authoritative for the committed EXT-token export.

bounded_static_reachability.method: Directed static traversal using committed direct-call, thunk, computed-call, and external edges; this is not runtime reachability.
bounded_static_reachability.runtime_reachability: UNOBSERVABLE; no original-binary trace or runtime validation is present.

queue_dependency_context.interpretation: These are static dependencies of queued engine-interface functions, not proof that the external targets are required by a reconstruction package or are gameplay logic.

gameplay_logic.assessment: Caller-category context exists for 7 known external targets, but external API names and caller labels do not establish gameplay logic. No delta row is promoted.

gameplay_support.assessment: Some external targets are called by gameplay-labeled functions, which is bounded dependency context only. It does not classify the target as gameplay support.

shared_state_root.assessment: No external row is itself a shared-state root. Reachable external targets are runtime dependencies on paths from canonical roots and do not establish state ownership.

important_engine_interface.curated_candidate_status: bounded external host/engine boundary adjacency; not an internal interface or gameplay claim
important_engine_interface.assessment: The 147 rows are external dependencies reached from engine-labeled callers; nine are additionally identified by the historical host-boundary index. None is an internal engine interface, and no importance claim is made from API names alone.

reconstruction_packages.assessment: No row is proven needed by a reconstruction package. Twelve known external targets are static dependencies of five queued engine-interface functions; this is not a package contract or runtime requirement.

canonical_function_boundary.vtable_scan_difference_interpretation: The vtable pass is a data-scan boundary, not a missing canonical executable function; no VA is absent from the function export or triage universe.

sdk_exact_address_boundary.interpretation: These are exact SDK-address and analysis-boundary records, not the 488 EXTERNAL manager entries. Contained and tail-alias repairs are not counted as new executable functions.

canonical_xref_boundary.interpretation: The external token namespace and the EXTERNAL manager namespace are different representations joined by the allowlist; the 488 are not 488 additional .text functions.

ghidra_state.interpretation: The current Ghidra state cannot confirm or refute stale-state explanations. The historical count is retained with its provenance and limitation rather than promoted to a fresh observation.

proven: The 488 difference is 488 distinct external manager entries outside the 58757 unique canonical executable-function VAs.
All 488 are external=true and canonical=false; 360 have allowlist identities and 128 are explicitly identity-unknown.
The canonical executable universe is 58757 and has zero missing VAs in the committed corpus and historical live observation.
The 488 do not have executable bodies, sections, body sizes, or persisted function contracts.
disproven: The 488 are not a same-address duplicate set in the committed export.
The 488 are not classified as internal thunk functions in the committed atlas.
The 488 are not 488 missing internal binary functions.
The triage-v4 versus triage-v6 classifier difference does not explain the count.
unobservable: Fresh live Ghidra manager identities and whether its external entries are synthetic placeholders or another manager representation.
External implementation semantics, generated/compiler origin, stub status, and semantic duplicate identity.
Runtime reachability and actual reconstruction-package requirements for the external entries.
Whether any external dependency is behaviorally important beyond the bounded static caller-context measurements.
overall_conclusion.decision: Retain 58757 as the executable-function denominator; report 488 separately as external-only manager scope, with 360 known identities, 128 unknown identities, 5479 joined external edges, and no gameplay/shared-state/interface/package promotion.

limitations: The current Ghidra bridge has no open program, so the historical 59245 manager count and 488 identities were not independently re-read live.
The semantic-atlas external-only records do not contain external implementation bodies, body sizes, containing blocks, thunk flags, stub flags, or generated classifications.
The 128 unknown external identities cannot be joined to the EXT-token xref allowlist and their reference use cannot be determined from the committed corpus.
Static xref reachability is not runtime reachability, execution order, dataflow, or object identity.
The separate 1186 SDK exact-address gap is an analysis-boundary issue and is not folded into the 488 count.
